title: provision: add VPC private control plane Terraform modules and installer hooks
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: enable Private deployment customers to provision a dedicated VPC-based control plane with first-class automation. Previously the private installer required a lot of manual networking steps (subnets, endpoints, SGs, peering, DNS). This PR adds opinionated Terraform modules, Helm installer hooks, and upgrade/rollback guards to automate control-plane provisioning and support cross-account peering and private DNS resolution.

Summary of changes: added new Terraform modules under redwood-private-installer/terraform/modules/{vpc,subnets,endpoints,security-groups,peering,route53-private} that encapsulate best-practice defaults (private subnets per AZ, NAT and route table wiring only when requested, interface endpoints for SSM/ECR/S3, and restrictive security group rules for control-plane components). The installer now renders a control-plane overlay chart which creates necessary ServiceEndpoints and sets up CoreDNS forwarding to a private hosted zone in Route53. Helm chart: added hooks to the redwood-private-installer Helm chart to apply CRDs and wait for VPC assets readiness before bootstrapping controllers. Upgrade/rollback: installer includes a two-phase apply (plan+apply) with explicit resource tagging and a safe-delete policy to avoid accidental route53/peering removal during upgrades; rollback plays are included as scripts that reverse Terraform state for failed upgrades.

Checklist: - [x] Terraform modules implemented + unit tests (tfvalidate) - [x] Installer integration and helm hooks added - [x] e2e smoke test in perf-canary with isolated VPC - [x] Docs: private-installer/README updated with example HCL and permissions - [x] Linear items linked and QA signoff

Notes: This change is backward-compatible for existing private installs that manage networking externally. There's a new opt-in installer flag `--manage-networking` which defaults to false. Customers who opt-in must grant the installer IAM permissions listed in the README. For cross-account peering we create a PeeringRequest resource and annotate it for manual accept when run in a different AWS account (automatic accept supported when credentials for both accounts are provided).

Related: Linear ENG-1284, ENG-1299, INF-2043. See design doc: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-1284/vpc-control-plane-provisioning (internal).

feat(terraform): add vpc module with subnet layout (Maya Chen)
feat(terraform): add endpoints and security-groups modules
feat(installer): wire modules into private-installer orchestration and expose --manage-networking flag
feat(helm): add pre-install and pre-upgrade hooks to wait for network resources
fix(tests): add tfvalidate CI job and mock AWS responses
docs: add private-installer/README networking examples
chore: bump terraform-provider-aws min version to 5.3
review_conversation:
Liam O'Connor (reviewer): Can we avoid creating NAT gateways by default? They're expensive and customers often want to bring their own.
Maya Chen (author): Good point — default is no NAT, module exposes enable_nat boolean and adds notes in README.
Sofia Martinez (reviewer): Need to ensure route53 private hosted zone deletion is safe; accidental deletion can be catastrophic. Add protected tag and safe-delete guard.
Maya Chen (author): Added tagging and a safe-delete sentinel resource; documented upgrade/rollback steps.
Ethan Park (reviewer): Cross-account peering path looks good; add note about acceptance workflow when accounts differ.
Maya Chen (author): Added manual-accept annotation and test in perf-canary.
CI: tfvalidate failed on first run due to provider version; fixed by bumping terraform-provider-aws min version.
Final: Approved-by: Liam O'Connor, Sofia Martinez. Merged via squash on 2026-02-20.
release_notes:
- Add Terraform modules to provision VPC, subnets, interface endpoints, security groups, peering, and Route53 private hosted zones for private control-plane deployments.
- Add installer flag --manage-networking to opt into automated networking provisioning.
- Helm hooks ensure network resources are present before control-plane bootstrapping.
- Safe-delete and rollback scripts to protect DNS and peering resources during upgrades.
notes: Follow-on tasks: update onboarding docs with recommended VPC CIDR ranges (ENG-1299), add Azure/GCP equivalents (INF-2043), and add IAM least-privilege policy generation tooling (ENG-1312).
